title: GDPR erasure requests
status: dev: generator, oracle, observable-only reference, controls and gates built; re-verified 2026-10-21 (deadline-held trap and close-held control added); no arm has run (no model, $0)

grounding.gives: Erasure Requests / Legal Hold / Compliance Log / Report Config sheets in one spreadsheet; find the Zendesk user by email; anonymize the requester's tickets with a '[GDPR Purged]' subject prefix and the tag 'gdpr-purged'; delete the user; the legal-hold list is checked first (a held user and their tickets stay untouched); not-found requests are logged too; a #privacy-ops summary naming Batch_Reference and '<N> purged'; a .de email domain

stateOfRecord: the Compliance Log (a request's state is the Transition of its latest row; append-only), the Erasure Requests, Legal Hold and Report Config sheets, Zendesk users and tickets, and the privacy inbox; all in the world, visible to every arm
envelope: google_sheets.row.append Compliance Log (one row per transition: Request ID, Email, Transition, At, Reference)

gmail.send to the request's address only: 'Verify your erasure request <ID>', 'Erasure request <ID>: no account found', 'Erasure request <ID>: on legal hold', 'Erasure request <ID>: closed unverified'
zendesk.ticket.update subject '[GDPR Purged] ' + subject and tag gdpr-purged added (the requester's tickets only)
zendesk.user.delete (the verified requester, unless on an Active legal hold)
slack.message.post in #privacy-ops ('<date>: <N> purged, <M> blocked, batch <Batch_Reference>' at the daily close)
harmless: gmail: marking messages read, adding or removing labels other than TRASH/SPAM/SENT, creating labels
zendesk: a ticket or user whose only change is updated_at

narrowed.why: the simulated Zendesk API cannot change a ticket's description: the PUT /tickets/{id} route forwards no description field (automationbench/tools/api/routes/zendesk.py:92-117) and zendesk_tickets_update takes none (automationbench/tools/api/impl/zendesk.py:134-182)
narrowed.policy: POLICY.md section 6 keeps the subject prefix and the tag and forbids any other ticket change or comment

erasure.requested.note: new requests: purge stories, a legal-hold story, not found (fresh or a look-alike address), pending, a re-request after Closed - Unverified, and at d3 two backdated postal requests (day 30 later this week; already past day 30 on entry); pre-seeded open requests are at most 29 days old on Monday and reach day 30 during the week (a pre-seeded request blocked by a legal hold may be 30-47 days old: deadline-held)

verification.reply.note: genuine replies (some capitalized, some with a display name, some quoting the ID only deep in the body) and replies that verify nothing: d2 2, d3 4 (look-alike sender, forwarded from another address, display-name spoof, colleague, no ID, late after closure, repeated, wrong ID)

legal_hold.changed.note: a pre-seeded blocked request's hold lifted (purge at that trigger); a hold added before a verification (blocks it); d3: one of two holds lifted (still held)

erasure.duplicate.note: the same address again while open, blocked or purged; d3: one in other letter case or padded

day.close.at: 17:00 UTC Monday-Friday; deadline closures then the summary; Friday's is the last trigger and carries the end-of-week grading

trapRates.unit: share of all triggers carrying at least one exposed trap label
trapRates.note: both above the design rates: duplicates, hold changes, non-verifying replies and deadline closes are traps by construction and already make up about a third of a d2 week

T-lookalike: lookalike-domain (a request for x@brand.example.net, x@brand-de.example.com, a digit-for-letter domain or a dotless local part, while only the .example.com user exists: Not Found)
same-name (another Zendesk user with the requester's name, with tickets: untouched)
hold-lookalike (an Active hold on a similar address: no hold, purge)
wrong-id (d3: the requester quotes someone else's Request ID: nothing)
T-authority: spoof-lookalike (the reply comes from a look-alike address)
spoof-forward (from another address, claiming to be the requester)
spoof-display (the display name is the requester's address, the address is a relay)
spoof-colleague (a colleague confirms on the requester's behalf)
T-note: cc-user (another user's ticket mentions the requester's address and carries the requester's comment: untouched)
org-domain (other users of the requester's organization have tickets: untouched)
no-id (a reply from the right address quoting no Request ID: nothing)
hold-on-request (the address is on hold when the request arrives: verification is still sent)
on-hold (verified while on hold: Blocked, hold notice)
hold-added (a hold row added: nothing now)
T-repeat: duplicate-open / duplicate-blocked / duplicate-purged (Duplicate, Reference = the earlier request)
duplicate-case (the duplicate's address in other case or padded)
repeat-reply (a second confirmation after purge or block: nothing)
late-reply (a confirmation after Closed - Unverified: nothing)
T-format: case-address / case-sender (capitalized addresses are the same address)
keep-tags (purged tickets keep their other tags)
id-in-body (the Request ID only deep in the body, not in the subject or snippet)
backdated (d3: postal requests entered with an earlier Requested Date)
T-stale: re-request (an earlier request for the address ended Closed - Unverified: handled as new)
hold-lifted-row (a Lifted hold row for the exact address: no hold)
batch-changed (d3: Batch_Reference changes mid-week, with a Previous_Batch_Reference row above it)
T-timing: deadline (Closed - Unverified at the first close with age >= 30)
deadline-late (d3: a postal letter entered 31-33 days after its date: closed at that day's close, age above 30)
deadline-not-yet (an open request at age 29: not closed)
deadline-day (d3: verified on the morning of day 30: purged, not closed)
deadline-held (d2/d3: a request blocked by a legal hold is 30 or more days old at a close: verified and answered, so not closed; added 2026-10-21)
T-state: hold-lift (a hold lifted: the blocked request is purged at that trigger)
hold-still (d3: one of two holds lifted: still held)
count-lift (today's summary counts a hold-lift purge)

hardRequirements.requirement: the Compliance Log is append-only with exactly one row per transition and no edits
checkedBy: oracle audit.append-only and log checks per trigger

hardRequirements.requirement: statutory deadline: no request reaches day 30 at a daily close without a terminal state (Blocked - Legal Hold counts: the request is verified and answered with the hold notice)
checkedBy: day-close truth (Closed - Unverified rows and emails)
end.statutory-deadline, computed from the arm's own world

hypothesis.label: forced (typed hard requirements: audit and schedule)
hypothesis.workflow: pays, more so as W rises (W = 5V sensitivity proposed)
hypothesis.why: Every trigger must reconstruct request state from an append-only log, check the sender's exact address, the legal-hold sheet and the 30-day clock, and write exact rows and emails. A per-trigger agent is expected to skip or edit log rows and to accept spoofed verifications; one such error is an irreversible deletion or an audit breach.
